clue.text: Guy showing anger interrupted by female copper

indicators.note: a word interrupted by others has them breaking into its middle

parts.note: to rile someone is to anger them
Di is a woman's name, standing for any female
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A man loses his temper when a policewoman breaks in on him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' is a verb here, to mock; 'copper' looks like a police officer but is the metal's symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: To guy someone is an old verb for teasing or mocking them, a synonym.

clue.text: Once again put away record in storage facility

indicators.note: in means the record goes inside the storage word

parts.note: a rack is a frame for storing things
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A vinyl record goes back on the shelf for storage.
explanation.definitionFit: To repack is to pack again, putting belongings away once more.

clue.text: One can't see part of the sailing equipment

definitions.meaning: a ... is one that has lost its sight
a round wooden block used in a ship's rigging

explanation.definitionFit: A blind eye is called dead, and a deadeye is a rigging block with holes for lanyards.

clue.text: Mad person in band of citizens, beast who goes on and on?

indicators.note: in means the mad person is placed within the band letters

parts.note: CB is Citizens' Band radio
the Mad Hatter from Alice in Wonderland
an ox is a beast of burden

explanation.surface: A lunatic in a citizens' band, a creature who never stops talking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band of citizens' looks like a group of people but is CB radio.
explanation.definitionFit: A chatterbox is someone who talks incessantly.

clue.text: Where top minister may be found capable at helm, though troubled

definitions.text: Where top minister may be found

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A capable leader at the helm of government still faces trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'top minister' is a churchman, not a politician: the Archbishop of Canterbury, whose London residence this is.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambeth Palace is the London home of the Archbishop of Canterbury, the senior Anglican cleric.

clue.text: Monsieur made point in funny language

indicators.note: Monsieur is made into point: the one letter is swapped for the other pair

parts.note: funny means comic

explanation.surface: A Frenchman tries to make his point in an amusing tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Coptic is the liturgical tongue of Egypt's Coptic Christian church.

clue.text: Line of appeal made to guerrilla fighter

parts.note: O is an exclamation of appeal, as in O Lord
Che Guevara was a famous guerrilla leader

explanation.surface: A line of appeal is put to a revolutionary.
explanation.walkthrough: The oche is the line a darts player stands behind when throwing.
explanation.definitionFit: In darts the throwing line on the floor is called the oche.

clue.text: Union body of jolly types means to reduce grinding disorder

parts.note: TU is a trade union
Royal Marines are nicknamed jollies, abbreviated RM
oil lubricates and reduces friction

explanation.surface: A union of cheerful types finds a way to ease a grinding mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jolly' is old naval slang for a Royal Marine, so the body is the RM.
explanation.definitionFit: Turmoil is a state of great confusion or upheaval.

clue.text: Club in church gathering round church guide

indicators.note: in means the club word sits inside the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: gathering round means enclosing, so the second church goes inside the club

parts.note: an iron is a golf club
CE again for the Church of England

explanation.surface: A club meets in a church, gathering round the church for a tour leader.
explanation.definitionFit: A cicerone is a guide who shows sightseers around, named after the orator Cicero.

clue.text: Organic matter mostly used for garden plant

indicators.note: mostly means all but the final letter of the word is kept

parts.note: peat is decayed organic matter dug from bogs

explanation.surface: Compost made of peat is spread around a vegetable patch.
explanation.definitionFit: The pea is a climbing legume commonly grown in gardens.

clue.text: Such is the pressure we're all under

definitions.text: Such is the pressure we're all under

parts.words: Such is the pressure we're all under
parts.note: the weight of air above us all is the pressure of the air around the planet, as measured in millibars

explanation.surface: A rueful remark about how stressed everyone is these days.
explanation.definitionFit: Air pressure pressing on everyone at the surface is described by the adjective for the planet's gaseous envelope.

clue.text: Replacement girl, one unequalled

parts.note: a stand-in is a substitute
gal is a colloquial word for girl
taken as written

explanation.surface: A substitute girl turns out to be unrivalled.
explanation.definitionFit: Being without equal is to stand apart, unmatched by any rival.

clue.text: Talk socially, as Jack couldn't (but his wife could)

definitions.meaning: to have a long idle gossip

definitions.text: as Jack couldn't (but his wife could)
definitions.meaning: the nursery rhyme says Jack Sprat could eat no fat and his wife could eat no lean, read literally as chomping on the fat

explanation.walkthrough: Jack Sprat is a nursery-rhyme man who ate only lean meat while his wife ate only fat.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to chat at length in a relaxed way, a colloquial phrase.

clue.text: Rude person's surprising exclamation meets resistance

parts.note: boo is what you shout to startle someone
R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A lout's startling shout meets opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: A boor is an ill-mannered, uncouth person, a synonym.

clue.text: Number having to be removed from shade burnt unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something has to be taken from a lampshade that unfortunately got scorched.
explanation.definitionFit: In arithmetic, the subtrahend is the quantity subtracted from another.

clue.text: Want diamonds? That's what the most demanding person wants

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for the card suit diamonds

parts.words: what the most demanding person wants
parts.note: the idiom says a greedy person wants the earth

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether you crave jewels, saying the greediest people want everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Want as a noun means lack or scarcity, the sense of a shortage.

clue.text: Mound of meal only half finished with drink left to be imbibed

indicators.note: imbibed means swallowed, so these letters go inside the other word
only half the word for the meal is finished, so its back three letters go

parts.note: dinner is an evening meal
rum is a spirit drink

explanation.surface: Someone leaves dinner half eaten but downs a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A drumlin is an elongated hill of glacial deposit, a kind of mound.

clue.text: Like one who may need a loan secured

definitions.text: Like one who may need a loan
definitions.meaning: short of money, as in ... for cash

explanation.definitionFit: Short of funds, and fastened down with a belt or band.

clue.text: Lottery with many about to collect large sum (not billions initially)

indicators.note: collect means gather in, so one piece goes inside the other
about means turned round, so the letters of the word for many run backwards

parts.note: a lot means many

indicators.note: not means the following letter is left out of the word for a big sum

parts.note: a bomb is slang for a large sum of money, as in costing a bomb

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word billions

explanation.surface: A lottery syndicate is about to scoop a big jackpot, though not billions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'large sum' is slang, as in costing a bomb; reversing the many-word gives TOLA, and the trimmed sum slots in after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A tombola is a raffle-style lottery where tickets are drawn from a drum, often at fetes.

clue.text: Author getting depressed in bad dream when night falls

indicators.note: in means the word for depressed goes inside
falls means drops away, so the word night is removed

parts.note: a nightmare is a bad dream
taken as written
low means depressed

explanation.surface: A writer feeling down has nightmares once darkness comes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when night falls' removes NIGHT from NIGHTMARE, leaving MARE for LOW to enter.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Marlowe was an Elizabethan dramatist and poet, author of Doctor Faustus.

clue.text: Resident is innocent but is given time inside

indicators.note: inside means the time letter is placed within the word for innocent

parts.note: naive means innocent or unworldly

explanation.surface: A local is innocent but still gets sent down for a stretch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given time' looks like a prison sentence but it puts T inside NAIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A native is someone born in and living in a place, an inhabitant.

clue.text: Very short edition introducing a set of books with a particular philosophy

parts.note: V is the short form of very
NT is the New Testament, a set of biblical books

explanation.surface: A very brief edition introduces a set of books with a special philosophy.
explanation.definitionFit: Vedanta is a school of Hindu philosophy based on the Upanishads.

clue.text: Oxford accent?

definitions.meaning: an Oxford is a style of laced shoe, like a stout walking shoe
a strong regional accent, especially Irish

explanation.walkthrough: 'Oxford accent' suggests a posh university voice, but it is two separate definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A brogue is a sturdy perforated shoe and also a thick Irish or Scottish accent.

clue.text: Astronomer's word for "light"

definitions.meaning: George ... was a nineteenth-century Astronomer Royal
light in the sense of breezy, delicate or well ventilated

explanation.walkthrough: The astronomer's name doubles as the adjective; 'word for' simply links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir George Airy was Astronomer Royal, and the adjective means delicate and weightless, like air.

clue.text: Fiery spirit turning very hot unfortunately, engulfing fellow

indicators.note: engulfing means swallowing up, so the word for fellow goes inside
turning means the two following words are read backwards together

parts.note: red hot, so red means very hot
alas is the exclamation meaning unfortunately
man means a fellow or chap

explanation.surface: An overheated, unlucky person gets spun round and swallows a bloke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses REDALAS into SALADER, and MAN goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: In folklore the salamander is an elemental spirit said to live in fire.

clue.text: Medicine bottle essential when the heart's failing

indicators.note: the heart is the central letter, and failing means it is lost

parts.note: vital means essential

explanation.surface: A bottle of medicine is crucial when someone's heart gives out.
explanation.definitionFit: A vial is a small glass bottle for medicine or liquids.

clue.text: Awfully poor trifle — last thing one needs for dessert

indicators.note: awfully suggests something badly done, so the letters are mixed up
last thing picks the final letter of the word one

explanation.surface: A dreadful trifle needs one final touch before serving as pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awfully' rearranges POOR TRIFLE into PROFITEROL, and E closes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A profiterole is a small cream-filled choux pastry bun served as a pudding.

clue.text: Component of anagram giving bother

indicators.note: a component is a part, so the answer is a run of letters inside the next word

explanation.surface: Part of a word puzzle gives the solver grief.
explanation.definitionFit: To nag is to pester or harass, a synonym of bother.

clue.text: Lives in road at end near cathedral city

indicators.note: at end picks the final letter of the word road

parts.note: Wells in Somerset is England's smallest cathedral city

explanation.surface: Someone lives at the end of a road close to a cathedral city.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell somewhere is to reside or make one's home there.

clue.text: Someone mistaking wife for a hat, say — or a helmet?

definitions.text: Someone mistaking wife for a hat, say
definitions.meaning: Oliver Sacks wrote of a man who mistook his wife for a hat, an extreme mental case; slang for a crazy person
a helmet is literally a protective covering for the head

explanation.walkthrough: The first half alludes to Oliver Sacks's book The Man Who Mistook His Wife for a Hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for an unhinged person, and literally a protective casing worn over the cranium.
